Mia is gone. Not frozen. Gone. Her spot on the street is empty.
Last time, Mia's phone died, and she froze.

text: You blink, and she just isn't there anymore.

Your phone buzzes. Your own number again. She's back at eleven fifty-eight.
You scroll up. Every text was sent from your phone. At times that haven't happened yet.
The static takes one step closer. Your battery, one percent.
One more text. When a phone dies, you start again. I know. I'm you.

text: Your hands shake. The texts were never from a stranger.
They were from you. And if you don't send them, nobody will.
Would you trust a text from yourself? Yes or no.
